Use this file for gaps discovered during project work that do not clearly belong
to the active project's own gap tracker. This is a repo-level surfacing and
routing file for cross-project, orphaned, or out-of-current-scope gaps.

When a living project is created or refreshed, check this file before creating
new gap rows. Import only the gaps that genuinely belong to the project after
critical scope review.

| GG-540 | open | physics_gap | One water (agora-257c, 2026-10-30): the flood that cuts the channel | `RIVER_FLOOD_TO_NORMAL_FLOW = 3` is a STATED input: the sources checked (Williams 1978 via the USACE and NC State channel-forming notes; NRCS) give the flood's return period (about 1.5 years) and say the mean flow is less, but no one ratio. 2026-11-02 (agora-257c): a derivation now exists, `riverChannel.ts` `riverFloodToNormalFlow`, and every river segment records it (`RiverSegmentWater.floodRatio`, from the mean climate of the river's own cells: FMG rainfall `prec` x 100 mm, temperature deg C). (3) Places next to each other share street, so groups overlap: 89 pairs stood closer than 0.5 m at 13:00 in the demo town (392 with the first 10 fixed spots). | Resolved 2026-11-02 (claude-npc-life). (1) `residentDoorUse` gets the town's graph from `groundAgentMotion.streetGraphForTown` (the crowd's own graph object), so errand legs open the home leaf (new test in `residentDoorUse.test.ts`). (2) The main cause was not the door connector: the street graph was split. A street that ends on another street's span shared no node with it, so the seed-42 town had 13 unjoined lanes and 838 of 3,886 legs (21.6%) fell back to a straight line through the buildings. `agentPath.joinStreetEnds` splits a span at each dead end within 2 ft; both towns now have one connected graph and 0 straight-line legs. | GG-472 | open | correctness | Remy directive 8491 rules audit (travel, time, survival) | Trips run nonstop with no 8-hour travel day, and the forced-march save is one roll for the whole trip. | Route time is miles / mph with nothing added (routePlanning.ts:177-185); MapPane.tsx:1057 uses it as clock time and passes it to deriveForcedMarch. Example: 100 miles at 3 mph -> clock +33h20m, 2 ration-days, one DC 35 CON save (10 + 25). By 5e: about 4.2 travel days of 8 hours, about 5 ration-days, no forced march; a long march needs one save per hour past 8 (DC 11, 12, ...), each failure one exhaustion level; resolveForcedMarch rolls once at the final DC.  Native follow-up 2026-10-31: Mara takes consecutive7h30 and10h6 legs after one rest; only the latter leg getsDC12, actual12+2=14pass. Tests for longbow, glaive, javelin.; Fixed 2026-10-25 by claude-agora-review. New src/utils/combat/weaponRange.ts: PHB range table keyed by base weapon id (name fallback for variants like 'Longbow +1'), case-insensitive property checks, isRangedWeapon (Ranged category or Ammunition), isThrownMeleeWeapon, reach tiles. createWeaponAbility (combatUtils.ts) gives ranged weapons their normal range (longbow 30 tiles = 150 ft), reach weapons 2 tiles, and adds a separate 'Throw <weapon>' ability (id attack_main_thrown) for thrown melee weapons; Frenzy and Divine Smite read reach the same way. WeaponAttackCommand decides ranged with isRangedWeaponAttack (weapon category, not range > 1), so a glaive keeps Strength, a bow uses Dexterity, a dart takes the better of Str/Dex, and a thrown melee weapon keeps its melee modifier; high-ground and Sneak Attack use the same check; ranged and thrown hits pass a 'ranged' marker so Savage Attacks no longer fires on them. Tests: weaponRange.test.ts (6) and 3 new mode tests in AbilityCommandFactory.weaponDamage.test.ts; 5 failed on the old code. 505 test files / 3563 tests pass across commands, combat, spells, Combat/BattleMap screens, state and devtools; scoped typecheck 0; lint 0 errors. Not done: long-range disadvantage between normal and long range, Loading and Ammunition use, and the off-hand attack (GG-497). Visual check DONE 2026-11-01 (claude-agora-review): on `?step=battlemap`, the Dev Player lab set to Monk (a quick character, which carries the class spear since GG-559) shows "Spear" (1 tile, 5 ft) and "Throw Spear" in the ability bar, and the Throw Spear tooltip reads "Range: 4 tiles (20 ft)", the spear's thrown normal range. Screenshot `.agent/scratch/gg495-monk/monk-throw-spear-20ft.jpg` (gitignored). The 60 ft long range is not shown in the UI, which matches the open long-range item above. (claude-agora-review, 2026-10-25) Long range DONE 2026-11-01 (claude-agora-review): `Ability.longRange` (tiles) is set on every ranged weapon and Throw attack from the PHB table (`weaponLongRangeTiles`); targeting (`useTargetValidator`, `useTargetSelection`) accepts targets out to the long range; the attack roll has Disadvantage between normal and long range, with a "(Long range)" log reason (`isAtLongRange` in AbilityCommandFactory, same distance measure as targeting); the ability button shows "4 tiles (20 ft), long 12 tiles (60 ft)". Tests: 3 in weaponRange.test.ts, 2 in AbilityCommandFactory.weaponDamage.test.ts (the Disadvantage test fails with the rule switched off). Seen on screen: quick Monk Throw Spear tooltip (`.agent/scratch/gg495-monk/monk-throw-spear-long-60ft.jpg`). AI long range DONE 2026-11-01 (claude-agora-review): `evaluateAttackPlan` in combatAI.ts accepts targets out to the long range; with no normal-range shot it builds a long-range attack plan whose damage counts at `LONG_RANGE_DAMAGE_FACTOR` (0.55, for Disadvantage) and picks it over moving into normal range only when it scores higher; the move-first step no longer walks away from a planned long-range shot. Tests: 3 in combatAI.test.ts (the rooted thrower throws at 40 ft; an equal normal-range target wins; a target past 60 ft is ignored); the first failed before the change. Long-range shading DONE 2026-11-01 (claude-agora-review): `computeLongRangeTargetSet` (useTargetSelection.ts) marks the valid target tiles past normal range and within long range, measuring creature to creature on an occupied tile (as the attack roll does) and creature to tile otherwise (as targeting does); BattleMapTile draws those tiles with the same rose color at a lower fill plus diagonal hatching (`data-overlay-kind="target-long-range"`), and the legend adds "Long Range (Disadvantage)". The targeting card also shows "long 12 tiles (60 ft)". Tests: useTargetSelection.longRange.test.ts (3) and a BattleMapTile overlay test. Seen on screen (headless Chrome on port 3000 with the HMR client stubbed, because shared-checkout edits reloaded the pane): quick Monk Throw Spear, Goblin at 15 ft solid fill, Orc at 40 ft hatched fill (`.agent/scratch/gg495-monk/long-range-band.png`, `long-range-band-zoom.png`); the enemies were moved next to the Monk through the preview board state for the capture. The 3D map (BattleMap3D TargetingDecals) draws the band as a fainter red frame (opacity 0.35 against 0.85), covered by a TargetingDecals test through its dev probe; the 3D band was not checked on screen. Found while fixing: player weapon hits never added the ability modifier to DAMAGE at all (only unarmed strikes did), so a Strength 16 longsword hit dealt 1d8, not 1d8+3. WeaponAttackCommand (AbilityCommandFactory.ts) now: (1) adds magicProperties.magicalBonus to the computed attack roll; (2) applyWeaponDamageBonus adds the attack's ability modifier (Str, finesse best, ranged Dex, or spellcasting via augment) plus the magic bonus to the damage dice as a flat term (crits double dice only); off-hand hits add the modifier only when negative; skipped when a held-weapon augment (Shillelagh, Magic Stone) already adds the spellcasting modifier, for monster attacks with a fixed attackBonus, and for unarmed strikes; (3) a +N weapon counts as magical. DamageCommand: Great Weapon Master now matches 'Heavy' case-insensitively (it never fired on item data). New AbilityCommandFactory.weaponDamage.test.ts (4 tests; 3 failed on the old code).
